document.summary: LptD proteins are the outer-membrane component of the lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) system of diderm bacteria. Each has an N-terminal periplasmic beta-jellyroll domain that joins the LptA bridge and a C-terminal 26-stranded beta-barrel that, with the plug lipoprotein LptE, forms the LptD/LptE translocon. LPS arriving through the bridge is released through a lateral opening of the barrel into the outer leaflet of the outer membrane. In Escherichia coli LptD (formerly Imp/OstA) is essential and was first noticed through mutations that increase outer-membrane permeability to organic solvents and antibiotics. The family is a single PANTHER subfamily and its distribution tracks diderm bacteria with an outer membrane.
document.coherence_reason: One subfamily (SF1) of LptD translocons. document.summary: This family contains LptF and LptG, the two paralogous transmembrane subunits of the LptB2FG ATP-binding cassette transporter that extracts lipopolysaccharide (LPS) from the outer leaflet of the inner membrane of diderm bacteria. LptF and LptG each have six transmembrane helices and a periplasmic beta-jellyroll domain; together they form a V-shaped cavity that LPS enters laterally from the membrane, and ATP hydrolysis by the cytoplasmic LptB dimer drives LPS out of the cavity into the LptC/LptA/LptD bridge. Both proteins are essential in Escherichia coli, where they were identified as the missing transmembrane components of the Lpt transporter (formerly YjgP and YjgQ). PANTHER separates the gammaproteobacterial LptF (SF7) and LptG (SF2) subfamilies from SF6 and SF8, which hold both paralogues from other phyla. The family name is taken from the Synechocystis member Slr0882.
document.coherence_reason: Every member is an LptF- or LptG-type permease. document.summary: LptA proteins are periplasmic beta-jellyroll proteins of the lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) system of diderm bacteria. Head-to-tail oligomers of LptA connect the beta-jellyroll of the inner-membrane protein LptC to the N-terminal beta-jellyroll of the outer-membrane translocon LptD, forming a continuous hydrophobic groove through which LPS molecules are pushed across the periplasm. In Escherichia coli LptA is essential, binds LPS, and its depletion causes LPS to accumulate in the inner membrane. The family consists of a single PANTHER subfamily and its members share this bridging role wherever the remaining Lpt components are present.
document.coherence_reason: One subfamily (SF1); every PAINT reference-tree member descends from the single IBD node PTN002194456, and characterized members (E. coli LptA, P. aeruginosa LptH) are Lpt bridge proteins.

document.summary: LptC proteins are bitopic inner-membrane proteins of the lipopolysaccharide transport (Lpt) system of diderm bacteria. A single N-terminal transmembrane helix inserts into the LptF/LptG transmembrane domains of the LptB2FG ABC transporter, and the periplasmic beta-jellyroll domain receives LPS extracted by LptB2FG and passes it to the LptA bridge, which leads to the outer-membrane translocon LptD/LptE. LptC is essential in Escherichia coli, where its depletion blocks LPS transport to the outer membrane. The family consists of a single PANTHER subfamily.

document.preferred_name: LivG/LivF/LptB-type ABC transporter ATP-binding protein family
document.summary: An ABC (ATP-binding cassette) nucleotide-binding-domain family of bacteria and archaea. All members are cytoplasmic ATPase subunits that dock onto the transmembrane domains of an inner-membrane ABC transporter and couple ATP binding and hydrolysis to transport. Two functionally distinct groups are well characterized. The LivG/LivF/BraF-type subunits (SF11, SF7 and related subfamilies) energize binding-protein-dependent uptake of branched-chain and other neutral amino acids. The LptB subfamily (SF10) energizes the LptB2FG transporter, which extracts lipopolysaccharide from the inner membrane and pushes it into the periplasmic Lpt bridge; LptB is essential in Escherichia coli, and ATP hydrolysis by LptB is required for LPS transport. Substrate and pathway therefore differ by subfamily, while ATPase activity and inner-membrane association are shared.
document.coherence_reason: The family lumps amino-acid uptake ATPases (LivG/LivF/BraF, SF11 and SF7; branched-chain amino acid ATPases of archaea, SF5 and SF8) with the LPS-export ATPase LptB (SF10). Transport substrate and direction cannot be propagated family-wide; only the ABC ATPase activity and membrane association are shared.
